citations.assessment: The narrative names Rava as the son of Rav Yosef bar Chama and distinguishes his father from the Rav Yosef he visits.
The passage is in Bava Batra, Yesh Nochalin, and has Rabbi Abba send the reported question to Rav Yosef bar Chama. Preserve פי״ג as transmitted.
The chain explicitly names Rav Yosef bar Chama citing Rabbi Oshaya.
This witness gives the dispute between Rabbi Yose bar Chama and Rabbi Zeira, or alternatively Rava son of Rav Yosef bar Chama and Rabbi Zeira. Preserve the first reading and Heilprin’s correction.
Rav Yosef bar Chama gives Rabbi Yochanan’s view on Rabbi Shimon, against Rami bar Chama’s citation of Rav Nachman.
Rav Yosef bar Chama and Rabbi Zeira give different rulings in the name of Rav Nachman.
Rav Yosef bar Chama transmits Rav Sheshet. The expanded patronymic involving Rabbah belongs to another locus.
The alternate chain at this locus is Rav Yosef bar Chama quoting Rav Sheshet.
The Bavli has Rabbah son of Yosef bar Chama as one attribution. Rif and Rosh omit Rabbah and read Rav Yosef bar Chama.
The printed Rosh reads Rav Yosef bar Chama in the alternate chain.
The printed Rif reads Rav Yosef bar Chama, independently supporting Heilprin’s comparison.
The Bavli gives Rav Yosef bar Chama or Rav Yose bar Abba as the questioner.
The dialogue names Rav Assi bar Chama addressing Rava and subsequently gives Rav Sheshet’s explanation. Heilprin’s name correction remains conjectural.
The text has Rav Yosef bar Chama raise the contradiction to Rabbah. The printed Heilprin addressee remains visible.
This is the same Gittin passage cited above, with both opposing transmissions.
